items.title: Authors Guild Joins Protests Challenging Change in Australian Copyright Law
items.excerpt: Under proposed Australian legislation it would be legal for AI companies to exploit any author's work if the training is conducted on Australian soil; the Authors Guild has joined local writers in opposing it.

items.title: Zachary Mason Chases the Ghost in the Machine
items.excerpt: In his speculative story collection, the computer-scientist novelist spins stories about relationships between humans and sentient AI.

items.title: SoA's position on generative AI 'remains unchanged' after backlash to Ethical AI Charter
items.excerpt: Society of Authors CEO Anna Ganley responds to member criticism of the Charter of Ethical AI Use in the Creative Industries, saying the society's stance on generative AI has not changed.

items.title: YouTube looks to expand into audiobooks
items.excerpt: Rampant audiobook piracy on YouTube via AI-generated audio versions is pushing publishers to offer legitimate ways to listen to audiobooks on the platform.

items.title: Apple is adding an AI chatbot to Pages, Keynote, and Numbers
items.excerpt: Apple's new intelligent assistant can draft and restructure content in Pages and organize data in Numbers, bringing an AI writing partner into its document apps.

items.title: Grok Says Its AI-Generated Version of 'The Odyssey' Is 'Not Historically Accurate'
items.excerpt: Months after Elon Musk declared xAI's AI-generated adaptation of Homer's epic would outclass Christopher Nolan's film, the Grok bot itself admitted defeat on accuracy.

items.title: How AI Changes the Fundamental Structure of the Classroom—Especially the Segregated Ones
items.excerpt: A book excerpt examining how ChatGPT-era AI tools reshape classrooms, and why the effects fall unevenly on segregated schools.

items.title: Dubious, seemingly AI-generated Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave guidebooks flood Amazon Japan
items.excerpt: Amazon Japan's self-publishing system lets anyone mass-produce apparently AI-generated strategy guides ('guideslop'), and reviews suggest buyers are being misled.

items.title: Japan's Ministry of Finance proposes shared manga platform with AI translation for global fans
items.excerpt: A government proposal would unite multiple manga publishers on one global platform using AI translation, alongside a requested 250 billion yen in publisher subsidies.

items.title: LINE Manga launches AI character chats and fan fiction feature for 'IPs approved by authors'
items.excerpt: One of Japan's major digital comic apps adds generative-AI chats with manga characters and AI fan fiction, limited to works whose creators have opted in.

items.title: Anthropic illegally trained Claude with Stanford professors' books
items.excerpt: At least 10 Stanford academics' books were among the pirated works covered by the $1.5 billion Anthropic copyright settlement.

items.title: BC Professor Sues OpenAI and Microsoft For Copyright Infringement over textbooks
items.excerpt: A Boston College finance professor is among six textbook authors suing OpenAI and Microsoft for using their copyrighted textbooks to train AI models.

items.title: Library and Archives Canada cracking down on AI books amid copyright threats
items.excerpt: Canada's ISBN agency now requires a human-author declaration and limits ISBNs for books primarily generated by AI, including text, illustration and translation.

items.title: "1시간이면 1권 OK"…AI가 쓴 '딸깍 소설'로 공모전 가도 될까
items.excerpt: AI로 한 시간 만에 쓴 '딸깍 소설' 투고가 출판사와 공모전에 넘쳐나며 출판업계의 AI 집필 검증 고민이 깊어지고 있다.
